# Visual calibration

Use when a broad refinement request leaves the intervention unclear. A clear local correction can proceed directly.

## Identify the difference

Recover the requested outcome, current identity, and protected content or behavior. Translate “more professional”, “enterprise”, or “more impactful” into a specific issue in this context. Ask when different interpretations would materially change identity or scope.

Locate the relationship that needs work:

| Need | Possible intervention |
|---|---|
| Important content has too little presence | Strengthen its scale, position, contrast, imagery, or relationship to the action |
| Several elements compete | Redistribute emphasis, grouping, and rhythm |
| The interface feels inconsistent or unfinished | Resolve type roles, alignment, treatments, states, and continuity |

Change the resources involved in that issue. Reducing visual competition does not require removing expression, and increasing presence does not require adding effects everywhere.

## Choose the intervention

A vivid event page's signup action can gain presence through its position and relationship to the ticket details, while the large image and color remain. A visual collection may need a different proportion between work and metadata to make its artifacts lead. A working queue may need quieter summary emphasis so records lead, while useful totals and density stay.

These address similar attention problems through different choices. Compare the affected relationship and preserved content, rather than treating a larger button, new font, or neutral palette as a preset improvement.

Keep wording protected in visual-only work. Report material copy issues separately; copy-only work preserves presentation.

## Compare

Use matching content, states, and widths when before/after evidence is available. Check the intended improvement and recognizable character retained. Verify affected behavior and access independently. Correct observed gaps and recheck them; report rendering-dependent expectations as unverified when tools are unavailable.

## Diagnose before changing the vocabulary

Capture the current task with real content if possible. Name one observable obstacle: a heading and every summary compete with the record list; a price is visually detached from its service; a long introduction hides the first useful action; a form loses entries after a correction. Then locate the cause. A long path to an action may be information order, rather than button color. Tiny rows may be a container sizing choice, rather than the font family.

Use a compact diagnosis in working notes: observation, task consequence, cause, proposed intervention, protected choices and proof to collect. For example: “At 390px, horizontal page overflow hides each record's action. The six-column grid imposes a minimum width. Stack secondary fields under the record identifier; preserve every value, status and calculation. Verify each record and action at 390px and desktop.” This is more actionable than “improve mobile responsiveness.”

Distinguish defect from preference. An unreadable foreground, unreachable button or wrong total has a concrete correction. A preference for quieter surfaces requires judging the product's identity and primary task. Do not dress the preference as an accessibility finding. Conversely, a strong brand does not excuse clipped text or invisible focus.

## Select a proportional intervention

Start with the owning relationship. If the problem is separation, adjust grouping and alignment before adding borders. If emphasis is flat, redistribute it rather than enlarging every role. If content is hard to read, test measure, leading, weight and actual font loading before replacing the family. If the task needs a side-by-side comparison, removing columns for a beautiful narrow screenshot can destroy utility.

For typography-only work, inventory each role before editing, keep the palette and region structure, and compare line wrapping with the exact original copy. Do not shorten a heading to make the new font fit. For a color correction, measure the relevant pairs including focus, selected and error states; preserve a meaningful accent where a compatible shade works. For a broad refinement, structural changes can be appropriate when the structure is the diagnosed cause.

Keep changes attributable. Resolve one class of cause, render, then decide whether a second is needed. Changing family, palette, layout, content and navigation together may create a pleasing result, but it makes preservation and cause difficult to assess. It also risks exceeding a focused request. Revert a change that adds novelty without improving the diagnosed task.

## Compare the same problem twice

Check the before and after at matching viewport, content, scroll position and state. A populated desktop view cannot validate an empty mobile state. Confirm that protected wording, records, routes, actions and brand resources remain. Then test the specific improvement: can the same long name be read, the same error corrected, or the same amount compared? A changed screenshot alone does not answer that.

For uncertain visual judgments, name what remains uncertain instead of assigning a score. “The primary action is now adjacent to the price and visible at 390px” is observed. “This will increase conversion” requires separate product evidence. If rendering is unavailable, record source changes and the exact pending check. Use [Review](review.md) when the task is diagnosis rather than implementation.
